title: CICAN Dublin Archive — Batch 067 candidate evidence packet

candidates.description_summary: Terraced two-bay three-storey house over raised basement, one of a group of five similar houses, now in multiple occupancy. M-profile slate roof with black clay ridge tiles, hipped to south behind parapet with granite coping; stepped brick chimneystacks; machine-made red Flemish-bond brick walls with granite plinth; gauged-brick flat-arched openings and replacement uPVC windows. Round-headed entrance with deep moulded surround and Doric doorcase; replacement timber door and fanlight. Extended concrete platform shared with neighbour to south, with three granite steps; original wrought-iron railings and matching pedestrian gate.
candidates.appraisal_summary: NIAH describes this as an important component of a terrace of seven tall red-brick houses from the late Georgian period. It appears to have been refaced with little original fabric remaining, but the terrace retains an early residential streetscape.

candidates.description_summary: Terraced two-bay three-storey house over raised basement, built as one of a pair and now in multiple occupancy. M-profile slate roof with black clay ridge tiles, hipped to north behind rebuilt parapet with granite coping; red Flemish-bond brick walls on granite plinth over rendered basement; gauged-brick flat-arched openings, replacement uPVC windows and rendered rear elevation. Elliptical-headed entrance with deep moulded surround, replacement timber door and plain glazed fanlight. Extended granite platform with four concrete steps, shared with adjoining house; replacement steel division and original wrought-iron railings.
candidates.appraisal_summary: NIAH describes this as one of a pair of houses that stand as the tallest structures on the terrace, abutted by a single-storey villa to the north. It dates from the late Georgian period and retains its overall composition despite loss of much external fabric.
